$comment: Narration, dialogue and on-screen notes with timings in seconds. speaker: narrator | noe | salizar | note. Subtitles (VTT/SRT) are generated from this file by scripts/build_subtitles.mjs.

voice.narrator: Warm, measured documentary voice, about 150 words per minute. Pauses at each full stop.
voice.noe: Early twenties, curious and slightly hesitant; this is his first question to a senior doctor.
voice.salizar: Confident and kind, with a small smile in the voice.

cues.speaker: narrator
cues.text: Every day, hospitals produce thousands of medical images.

cues.speaker: narrator
cues.text: Each one holds information that could change someone's life.

cues.speaker: narrator
cues.text: This is Noé.

cues.speaker: narrator
cues.text: He works weekends at a university hospital, helping radiologists organize and review X-rays, CT scans, and MRI images.

cues.speaker: noe
cues.text: (to himself) How does anyone review all of this carefully?

cues.speaker: noe
cues.text: With so many images every day... how do you make sure nothing important is missed?

cues.speaker: salizar
cues.text: That's exactly why we're developing something new.

cues.speaker: narrator
cues.text: RadiologyML is an artificial intelligence system designed to help doctors identify patterns in medical images.

cues.speaker: narrator
cues.text: Instead of examining every image from scratch, it learns patterns from examples that experts have already reviewed.

cues.speaker: note
cues.text: RadiologyML is fictional. Its score is a model output, not a diagnosis.

cues.speaker: narrator
cues.text: To a machine, an image begins as numbers.

cues.speaker: narrator
cues.text: During training, a model learns patterns in those numbers that can help distinguish one type of image from another.

cues.speaker: narrator
cues.text: The more useful the training examples and feedback, the better the model may become at recognizing relevant patterns.

cues.speaker: narrator
cues.text: Machine learning models can make mistakes.

cues.speaker: narrator
cues.text: Doctors review their predictions, identify errors, and provide expert feedback.

cues.speaker: narrator
cues.text: After careful validation, those corrections can help researchers improve future versions of the model.

cues.speaker: narrator
cues.text: One day, the system flags an unusual pattern.

cues.speaker: narrator
cues.text: Dr. Salizar sends the image to a specialist, who confirms that the finding needs urgent attention.

cues.speaker: narrator
cues.text: The technology hasn't replaced the doctor. It has helped the medical team notice something important sooner.

cues.speaker: narrator
cues.text: But this raises a bigger question.

cues.speaker: narrator
cues.text: How can a computer learn from examples?

cues.speaker: narrator
cues.text: How does it recognize patterns, make predictions, and improve its performance?

cues.speaker: narrator
cues.text: Welcome to Machine Learning.
